name: Deuruxolitinib

what.text: Deuruxolitinib is a Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor taken by mouth. In lab tests it blocked JAK1, JAK2 and TYK2 more strongly than JAK3. How this relates to its effect is not known.

It treats alopecia areata, an autoimmune disease in which the immune system attacks hair follicles. It is not a treatment for male pattern hair loss. It was developed as CTP-543 by Concert Pharmaceuticals, later bought by Sun Pharmaceutical.

src.label: King et al., J Am Acad Dermatol (THRIVE-AA1)

research.text: Two Phase 3 trials (THRIVE-AA1 and THRIVE-AA2) in 1,209 adults aged 18 to 65 with at least 50% scalp hair loss supported approval. Each lasted 24 weeks. Both were run by Concert Pharmaceuticals.

research.meta: North America and Europe · 2024 · Randomized Phase III
research.title: THRIVE-AA1 (King et al.)

facts.v: 706 adults aged 18 to 65 with at least 50% scalp hair loss
deuruxolitinib 8 mg twice a day, 12 mg twice a day (not approved), or placebo
share with SALT 20 or less (80% or more scalp hair) at week 24

research.found: 29.6% on 8 mg and 41.5% on 12 mg reached SALT 20 or less, vs 0.8% on placebo. Most adverse events were mild or moderate. Several authors have ties to the developers.

src.label: King et al., J Am Acad Dermatol (THRIVE-AA1)

research.meta: Europe and North America · 2026 · Randomized Phase III
research.title: THRIVE-AA2 (Tsianakas et al.)

facts.v: 517 adults aged 18 to 65 with SALT 50 or more for at least 6 months
deuruxolitinib 12 mg twice a day, 8 mg twice a day, or placebo
share with SALT 20 or less at week 24

research.found: 33.0% on 8 mg and 38.3% on 12 mg reached SALT 20 or less, vs 0.8% on placebo. The authors say long-term effects and how long the response lasts were not assessed.

src.label: Tsianakas et al., J Am Acad Dermatol (THRIVE-AA2)

research.title: Twice-daily vs once-daily dosing (King et al.)

facts.v: randomized Phase 2 trial (NCT03811912) comparing two schedules
deuruxolitinib 8 mg twice a day or 16 mg once a day

research.found: SALT score improved by 46.4% with 8 mg twice a day vs 18.0% with 16 mg once a day. Adverse events were mild or moderate. The authors note the small size.

us.text: FDA approved deuruxolitinib as Leqselvi on July 25, 2024, for severe alopecia areata in adults. It has a boxed warning. It is not approved for male pattern hair loss or for people under 18. As of November 1, 2026.

after.title: Sport
after.text: Deuruxolitinib is not named on the WADA 2026 Prohibited List or on the 2027 List, which takes effect January 1, 2027. It is approved for human use, so class S0 (non-approved substances) does not cover it.

side.text: Leqselvi has a boxed warning for serious infections, death, cancer, major heart events and blood clots. It must not be used in people whose bodies clear it slowly (CYP2C9 poor metabolizers). Common side effects include headache, acne and raised muscle enzyme.

items.text: higher risk of serious infections, including tuberculosis, that can lead to hospitalization or death. Malignancies have occurred in people taking Leqselvi. Another JAK inhibitor had higher rates of death, lymphoma, lung cancer, major heart events and blood clots than TNF blockers in rheumatoid arthritis. Blood clots have occurred with Leqselvi.

headache, acne, nasopharyngitis, raised creatine kinase, high blood fats, tiredness, weight gain, low lymphocytes, high platelets, anemia, skin and soft tissue infections, low neutrophils and herpes infections.
people who are CYP2C9 poor metabolizers, or who take moderate or strong CYP2C9 inhibitors, have a higher risk of serious side effects and must not take it.
tears in the stomach or bowel (gastrointestinal perforations), low blood sugar in people with diabetes, and changes in blood fats and blood counts. Live vaccines should be avoided.

unconfirmed: The UK approval date for Leqselvi is taken from MHRA's press release (first published March 12, 2026); the exact licence date was not confirmed in MHRA's product database.
TGA's Product Information search found no deuruxolitinib document, but the Australian Register of Therapeutic Goods itself could not be searched, so Australian status is not confirmed.
Whether Leqselvi has been filed with EMA was not checked.
surprises: Leqselvi requires a genetic test (CYP2C9) before use, yet its label says no FDA-cleared or approved test for that purpose is currently available.
The UK approved deuruxolitinib in 2026, while no EU-wide authorisation was found.
